findings.reason: a node implementing the rule as written will carry stale generated content forward on exactly the pre-marker records that motivated the section, and the plan needs either a bound on the legacy rule or this as a stated residual with a case.
findings.text: the deliverable justifies the data-evidence-origin mark by saying it stops a stale generated section from being republished, but for a pre-marker record the legacy rule treats any unmarked section whose id is "none of the ids a synthesis can produce" as appended and carries it forward. Two routine ways an id stops being producible while its unmarked generated section remains on the record: (a) the section is deleted from the plan, so its authored id is absent from `_section_labels(source)` and, with no comments or runs left, absent from `available = set(comments_by_section) | set(runs_by_section)` (reckon/evidence.py:337-353); (b) a ledger run's `section` key, which `_render_document` renders as a section of that id (line ~372), is no longer returned for the plan. In both, the legacy rule carries the unmarked generated section forward as though an append had written it. The plan names only the opposite misclassification (a pre-marker append replaced by a rendered section) and only the plan-section-id drop case (s9), so this republish path is neither covered by a case nor stated as a residual.
